kernels.definition: Synovial joints are common movable joints with a joint cavity, articular cartilage, synovial fluid, and supporting ligaments that allow smooth motion.

definitionAnchor.quote: Synovial joints allow for smooth movements between the adjacent bones

facts.text: A key structural feature of a synovial joint is a fluid-filled joint cavity.

anchor.quote: A key structural characteristic for a synovial joint that is not seen at fibrous or cartilaginous joints is the presence of a joint cavity

facts.text: Ligaments support synovial joints by holding bones together and resisting abnormal motion.

anchor.quote: Ligaments support the joint by holding the bones together and resisting excess or abnormal joint motions

kernels.definition: Muscle tissue includes skeletal, cardiac, and smooth muscle; all are excitable, and contractility lets muscle pull on attachment points and shorten with force.

definitionAnchor.quote: the body contains three types of muscle tissue: skeletal muscle, cardiac muscle, and smooth muscle

facts.text: All three muscle tissue types share excitability.

anchor.quote: they all exhibit a quality called excitability

facts.text: Skeletal muscle depends on nervous-system signaling to work properly.

anchor.quote: skeletal muscle completely depends on signaling from the nervous system to work properly

kernels.definition: Nervous tissue is excitable tissue made mainly of neurons and neuroglia; neurons propagate information through electrochemical impulses called action potentials.

definitionAnchor.quote: Two main classes of cells make up nervous tissue: the neuron and neuroglia

facts.text: Nervous tissue sends and receives electrochemical signals that provide the body with information.

anchor.quote: capable of sending and receiving electrochemical signals that provide the body with information

facts.text: Neuroglia support neurons and modulate information propagation.

anchor.quote: Neuroglia play an essential role in supporting neurons and modulating their information propagation

kernels.definition: Sensory receptors detect internal or external stimuli and convert them into nervous-system signals; perception is the central processing of those signals into meaningful patterns.

definitionAnchor.quote: Perception is the central processing of sensory stimuli into a meaningful pattern

facts.text: Receptors are cells or structures that detect sensations.

anchor.quote: Receptors are the cells or structures that detect sensations

facts.text: Stimuli are changed into electrochemical signals of the nervous system.

anchor.quote: Stimuli from varying sources, and of different types, are received and changed into the electrochemical signals of the nervous system

kernels.definition: Hormones circulate through the bloodstream but affect only target cells with the appropriate receptors, triggering target-cell responses that regulate physiological processes.

definitionAnchor.quote: it will affect the activity only of its target cells; that is, cells with receptors for that particular hormone

facts.text: Hormone binding initiates a chain of events that leads to a target-cell response.

anchor.quote: Once the hormone binds to the receptor, a chain of events is initiated that leads to the target cell's response

facts.text: Hormones regulate processes including growth, metabolism, fluid balance, electrolyte balance, and sleep.

anchor.quote: metabolism, fluid, and electrolyte balance, sleep, and many other body functions

mcItems.q: Which structural element is essential for allowing smooth motion in a joint type characterized by a joint cavity?
mcItems.ex: The fluid-filled joint cavity is a key structural feature of a synovial joint that allows for smooth motion.

mcItems.q: Which statement accurately describes the action of circulating chemical messengers in the body?
op: Chemical messengers only influence cells possessing specific receptors.
Chemical messengers circulate in the blood and trigger responses in target cells.
Chemical messengers directly alter the structure of the target cell.
Chemical messengers only regulate growth and metabolism.
mcItems.ex: Chemical messengers circulate in the blood and trigger responses in target cells. This is correct because hormones circulate through the bloodstream but affect only target cells with the appropriate receptors, triggering target-cell responses that regulate physiological processes.

The substance initiates a sequence leading to a cellular reaction.
The substance alters the cell's internal structure directly.
The substance only affects processes like sleep and fluid balance.
mcItems.ex: The substance initiates a sequence leading to a cellular reaction. Hormone binding initiates a chain of events that leads to a target-cell response.

keyTerms.eg: Insulin circulates in the blood to regulate blood glucose levels in muscle cells.
keyTerms.mi: Circulating chemical messengers directly change the physical shape of the target cell.
keyTerms.cx: Circulating chemical messengers affect only target cells with the appropriate receptors.

keyTerms.df: The resulting action taken by a cell after receiving a signal.
keyTerms.eg: The liver increases glycogen storage in response to a circulating hormone signal.
keyTerms.mi: Target-cell response is the initial binding event itself.
keyTerms.cx: Target-cell response is the outcome of hormone binding initiating a chain of events.
